greek_phrase: Ἐν ἀρχῇ
chosen_rendering: in the beginning
alternate_renderings: in beginning; at the beginning; at first
rationale: Matches the Greek en + dative opening formula and preserves the canonical beginning-language without narrowing it to a point-location sense.

greek_phrase: ἐποίησεν
chosen_rendering: made
alternate_renderings: did; fashioned
rationale: Keeps the verb broad and direct without importing later technical wording. Direct Logos export shows NETS and LES and LES2 keep made rather than narrowing to created.

greek_phrase: τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν
chosen_rendering: heaven and earth
alternate_renderings: the sky and the earth; sky and land
rationale: In this paired expression the phrase works as a cosmic merism, so heaven and earth carries the full range better. Direct Logos export shows the LXX English witnesses stay close to this heaven-and-earth pair.

greek_phrase: ἀόρατος καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος
chosen_rendering: unseen and unformed
alternate_renderings: invisible and unprepared; unformed and unready
rationale: Preserves the double description and keeps the line concrete.

greek_phrase: σκότος ἐπάνω τῆς ἀβύσσου
chosen_rendering: darkness was over the abyss
alternate_renderings: darkness lay over the abyss; darkness was over the deep
rationale: Abyss stays closer to abyssos while the clause remains plain and unforced.

greek_phrase: πνεῦμα Θεοῦ ἐπεφέρετο
morphology: nominative noun + genitive noun + imperfect middle/passive 3 singular
chosen_rendering: the Spirit of God moved
alternate_renderings: a wind from God was moving; God's breath-wind moved
rationale: In this creation context, both the Hebrew and the Greek are best taken as Spirit rather than merely meteorological wind. Local Logos word-sense evidence also supports Spirit of God here rather than wind.

greek_phrase: ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος
chosen_rendering: over the water
alternate_renderings: above the waters
rationale: Greek uses singular hydatos as a mass noun here.

greek_phrase: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός
morphology: conjunction + aorist active indicative 3 singular + nominative noun
chosen_rendering: and God said
alternate_renderings: then God said
rationale: Keeps the repeated narrative cadence visible from clause to clause.

greek_phrase: γενηθήτω φῶς
morphology: aorist passive imperative 3 singular + nominative noun
chosen_rendering: let light come to be
alternate_renderings: let there be light; let light be
rationale: Keeps the force of ginomai instead of flattening it into bare existence.

greek_phrase: καὶ ἐγένετο φῶς
morphology: aorist middle indicative 3 singular + nominative noun
chosen_rendering: and light came to be
alternate_renderings: and there was light
rationale: Echoes the command verbally and keeps the narrative rhythm.

greek_phrase: ὅτι καλόν
chosen_rendering: that it was good
alternate_renderings: that it was fitting; that it was beautiful
rationale: Keeps the clause direct and leaves καλός broad enough to carry value beyond mere utility.

greek_phrase: διεχώρισεν
chosen_rendering: separated
alternate_renderings: divided; marked off
rationale: Plain English fits the decisive act without losing force.

greek_phrase: ἐκάλεσεν ἡμέραν / νύκτα
morphology: aorist active indicative + accusative predicate objects
chosen_rendering: called Day / called Night
alternate_renderings: named Day / named Night
rationale: Keeps naming language visible and preserves the paired cadence. Direct Logos export shows the LXX English witnesses staying close to the naming formula here.

greek_phrase: ἡμέρα μία
chosen_rendering: day one
alternate_renderings: first day
rationale: Keeps the cardinal wording visible instead of smoothing immediately to an ordinal. Direct Logos export confirms the witness split and supports keeping the Greek cardinal force visible.

greek_phrase: στερέωμα
chosen_rendering: firm span
alternate_renderings: expanse; firmament; vault
rationale: Fresh English keeps the idea of something set firm without importing older church diction whole.

greek_phrase: ἔστω διαχωρίζον
chosen_rendering: let it divide
alternate_renderings: let it be dividing; let it separate
rationale: Readable English keeps the functional force of the participle.

greek_phrase: ὑποκάτω / ἐπάνω
chosen_rendering: below / above
alternate_renderings: under / over
rationale: Short pair preserves the spatial contrast cleanly.

greek_phrase: οὐρανόν
chosen_rendering: Heaven
alternate_renderings: sky
rationale: In this naming line Heaven better matches the world-ordering register already set in verse 1.

greek_phrase: ἡμέρα δευτέρα
chosen_rendering: second day
alternate_renderings: day two
rationale: Greek shifts to an ordinal here, so English should show that shift.

greek_phrase: συναγωγὴν μίαν
chosen_rendering: one gathering
alternate_renderings: one place; one collection
rationale: Keeps the gathering image alive instead of flattening it into a generic place.

greek_phrase: ὀφθήτω ἡ ξηρά
chosen_rendering: let the dry land appear
alternate_renderings: let dry ground be seen
rationale: Keeps the emergence image visible.

greek_phrase: τὴν ξηρὰν γῆν
chosen_rendering: dry land
alternate_renderings: earth; dry ground
rationale: Dry land fits the named feature in context before Earth appears as the given name.

greek_phrase: τὰ συστήματα τῶν ὑδάτων
chosen_rendering: the gathered waters
alternate_renderings: the gathered systems of the waters; water-masses; collections of waters
rationale: Readable English compresses the phrase, while the footnote can preserve the fuller lexical picture.

greek_phrase: κατὰ γένος καὶ καθ᾿ ὁμοιότητα
chosen_rendering: according to kind and likeness
alternate_renderings: according to kind and according to form; by kind and resemblance
rationale: Keeps both terms visible instead of collapsing the second into a duplicate.

greek_phrase: ἐξήνεγκεν
chosen_rendering: brought forth
alternate_renderings: brought out; produced
rationale: Fits the earth-as-source imagery without sounding mechanical.

greek_phrase: ἡμέρα τρίτη
chosen_rendering: third day
alternate_renderings: day three
rationale: Keeps the ordinal sequence explicit.

greek_phrase: φωστῆρες
chosen_rendering: light-bearers
alternate_renderings: lights; luminaries
rationale: Fresh English preserves the sense of bodies that bear or give light.

greek_phrase: ὥστε φαίνειν
chosen_rendering: so as to shine
alternate_renderings: to give light; to shine
rationale: Keeps the purpose-result nuance of the clause.

greek_phrase: εἰς ἀρχὰς τῆς ἡμέρας / τῆς νυκτός
chosen_rendering: for the dominion of the day / night
alternate_renderings: for rule over the day / night; for the beginnings of the day / night
rationale: Dominion keeps the governing sense alive while marking that the Greek uses a noun rather than a verb.

greek_phrase: ἔθετο
chosen_rendering: placed
alternate_renderings: set; positioned
rationale: Simple English fits the ordered-placement scene.

greek_phrase: ἄρχειν
chosen_rendering: rule
alternate_renderings: govern
rationale: Short verb matches the functional role of the lights.

greek_phrase: ἑρπετὰ ψυχῶν ζωσῶν
chosen_rendering: swarming living creatures
alternate_renderings: creeping living things; crawling creatures with life
rationale: Swarming catches broader life-in-motion better than a narrow reptile sense.

greek_phrase: κήτη τὰ μεγάλα
chosen_rendering: great sea-creatures
alternate_renderings: great sea monsters; great marine creatures
rationale: Sea-creatures stays broad without muting the scale.

greek_phrase: αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε
chosen_rendering: increase and multiply
alternate_renderings: grow and multiply
rationale: Keeps the blessing formula recognizable.

greek_phrase: ψυχὴν ζῶσαν
chosen_rendering: living creatures
alternate_renderings: living being; living soul
rationale: Plural English reads naturally while preserving animate life.

greek_phrase: κτήνη
chosen_rendering: livestock
alternate_renderings: cattle; domestic animals
rationale: Livestock fits modern English while keeping domesticated-animal sense.

greek_phrase: ἄνθρωπον
chosen_rendering: humankind
alternate_renderings: human; the human
rationale: Collective English handles the verse's singular-to-plural shift best. Direct Logos export shows NETS and LES and LES2 all support this collective singular-to-plural movement better than a flat individual noun.

greek_phrase: κατ᾿ εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ᾿ ὁμοίωσιν
chosen_rendering: according to our image and according to likeness
alternate_renderings: in our image and likeness
rationale: Keeps both nouns audible instead of collapsing them too quickly. Direct Logos export shows NETS and LES and LES2 all preserve the pair rather than reducing it to one blended phrase.

greek_phrase: ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ
chosen_rendering: male and female
alternate_renderings: man and woman
rationale: Closer to the paired sex terms used in the Greek line.

greek_phrase: κατακυριεύσατε
chosen_rendering: subdue
alternate_renderings: bring under rule; master
rationale: Subdue preserves the stronger force of the compound verb.

greek_phrase: χόρτον σπόριμον σπεῖρον σπέρμα
chosen_rendering: seed-bearing plant that sows seed
alternate_renderings: every seed-bearing herb; every seeding plant
rationale: Keeps the reproductive wording foregrounded.

greek_phrase: ψυχὴν ζωῆς
chosen_rendering: living breath
alternate_renderings: living soul; life-breath
rationale: Living breath keeps animate vitality visible without overly theological loading.

greek_phrase: καλά λίαν
chosen_rendering: very good
alternate_renderings: exceedingly good; very fitting
rationale: Simple English captures the climactic intensification.

greek_phrase: κόσμος
chosen_rendering: ordered array
alternate_renderings: world; ornament; order
rationale: Ordered array keeps the sense of an arranged totality without importing modern planet-language too quickly.

greek_phrase: ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἕκτῃ
chosen_rendering: on the sixth day
alternate_renderings: on day six; in the sixth day
rationale: Keeps the Greek reading visible at a key textual point.

greek_phrase: κατέπαυσε
chosen_rendering: rested
alternate_renderings: ceased; stopped
rationale: Rested is natural English, while the footnote can preserve cessation nuance if needed.

greek_phrase: ἡγίασεν
chosen_rendering: made it holy
alternate_renderings: sanctified it; hallowed it
rationale: Plain English keeps the consecration idea readable.

greek_phrase: ὧν ἤρξατο ὁ Θεὸς ποιῆσαι
chosen_rendering: the works God had begun to make
alternate_renderings: which God began to make
rationale: Keeps the odd final wording audible rather than smoothing it away.

greek_phrase: βίβλος γενέσεως
chosen_rendering: the book of the origin
alternate_renderings: the book of the genesis; the record of origins; the account of becoming
rationale: Origin reads more naturally in English while still preserving the heading's source-language force.

greek_phrase: ἄνθρωπος οὐκ ἦν ἐργάζεσθαι αὐτήν
chosen_rendering: there was no human to work it
alternate_renderings: no one was there to cultivate it
rationale: Keeps the labor motif visible before the formed human appears.

greek_phrase: πηγή
chosen_rendering: spring
alternate_renderings: mist; fountain; water source
rationale: Spring fits the rising-water image better than a vague mist for now.

greek_phrase: ἔπλασεν
chosen_rendering: formed
alternate_renderings: fashioned; shaped
rationale: Formed keeps the hands-on shaping image clear. Direct Logos export shows NETS and LES and LES2 and SAAS all keep formed-language here.

greek_phrase: πνοὴν ζωῆς
chosen_rendering: the breath of life
alternate_renderings: breath of living; life-breath
rationale: Classic phrase but still direct and concrete. Direct Logos export shows no pressure to revise this line.

greek_phrase: εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν
chosen_rendering: a living soul
alternate_renderings: a living being; a living creature
rationale: The phrase is kept as living soul because it is direct Greek wording and stands behind the New Testament echo in 1 Corinthians 15:45. Direct Logos export also shows LES and LES2 and SAAS keep living soul rather than generalizing it.

greek_phrase: παράδεισον
chosen_rendering: garden
alternate_renderings: park; paradise
rationale: Garden reads naturally while remaining open to richer park imagery in notes.

greek_phrase: τὸ ξύλον τοῦ εἰδέναι γνωστὸν καλοῦ καὶ πονηροῦ
chosen_rendering: the tree of knowing good and evil
alternate_renderings: the tree of knowing what is known of good and evil
rationale: The Greek is odd, but this draft keeps the familiar core without pretending the syntax is simple.

greek_phrase: εἰς τέσσαρας ἀρχάς
chosen_rendering: into four heads
alternate_renderings: into four sources; into four branches
rationale: Heads is traditional and maps well to river-head language.

greek_phrase: βοηθὸν κατ᾿ αὐτόν
chosen_rendering: a helper corresponding to him
alternate_renderings: a helper fit for him; a helper matching him
rationale: Corresponding keeps the relational sense without flattening it into mere utility.

greek_phrase: ἔκστασιν / πλευρῶν
chosen_rendering: ecstasy / sides
alternate_renderings: deep sleep / ribs
rationale: This draft keeps the Greek's stronger trance-language and the broader side-image alive for now.

greek_phrase: γυνή / ἀνήρ
chosen_rendering: woman / man
alternate_renderings: wife / husband
rationale: This draft keeps the wordplay visible, even though the Greek phrase remains slightly awkward in English.

greek_phrase: φρονιμώτατος
chosen_rendering: the most shrewd
alternate_renderings: the most prudent; the most crafty
rationale: Shrewd keeps the intelligence sense while fitting the serpent's adversarial role better than prudent.

greek_phrase: τηρήσει κεφαλήν / πτέρναν
chosen_rendering: watch your head / watch his heel
alternate_renderings: strike your head / strike his heel; keep your head / keep his heel
rationale: The Greek verb is not the usual verb for crushing, so the draft keeps a more cautious rendering pending further review.

greek_phrase: ἡ ἀποστροφή σου
chosen_rendering: your turning
alternate_renderings: your desire; your return
rationale: Turning stays closest to the Greek noun and avoids importing later traditional wording too quickly.

greek_phrase: χιτῶνας δερματίνους
chosen_rendering: skin tunics
alternate_renderings: garments of skin; leather tunics
rationale: Skin tunics is plain, concrete, and close to the Greek image.

greek_phrase: πᾶσαι ψυχαί
chosen_rendering: persons
alternate_renderings: souls; lives
rationale: Persons fits headcount language here without forcing later metaphysical weight onto the census line.

greek_phrase: χυδαῖοι ἐγένοντο
chosen_rendering: became numerous
alternate_renderings: became common; became many
rationale: Numerous keeps the population-growth sense without the pejorative drift common can carry in English.

greek_phrase: ἐπληθύνεν δὲ ἡ γῆ αὐτούς
chosen_rendering: the land multiplied them
alternate_renderings: the land filled up with them; the land was full of them
rationale: Keeps the startling active Greek while leaving room for a smoother contextual rendering later if needed.

greek_phrase: κατασοφισώμεθα αὐτούς
chosen_rendering: deal shrewdly with them
alternate_renderings: deal craftily with them; outwit them
rationale: Preserves the wisdom-root while making the hostile policy unmistakable.

greek_phrase: κατωδύνων αὐτῶν τὴν ζωήν
chosen_rendering: made their life bitter
alternate_renderings: embittered their life
rationale: Keeps the bittering image explicit and concrete.

greek_phrase: ἐποίησαν ἑαυταῖς οἰκίας
chosen_rendering: established households for themselves
alternate_renderings: made houses for themselves; established families for themselves
rationale: Reads as household-establishment rather than literal construction while preserving the reflexive Greek.

greek_phrase: θίβιν
chosen_rendering: basket
alternate_renderings: ark; box
rationale: Basket reads naturally while leaving room to note the unusual loanword rather than forcing a heavier symbolic term into the line.

greek_phrase: ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος αὐτὸν ἀνειλόμην
chosen_rendering: I drew him out of the water
alternate_renderings: I took him up out of the water
rationale: Keeps Pharaoh's daughter's naming explanation explicit and concrete.

greek_phrase: μέγας γενόμενος
chosen_rendering: grown great
alternate_renderings: grown up; become great
rationale: Grown great keeps both age and stature in view, not merely physical adulthood.

greek_phrase: κατῳκίσθη...παρὰ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ
chosen_rendering: settled with the man
alternate_renderings: was established with the man; dwelt with the man
rationale: Settled keeps the durable placement sense without sounding overly formal.

greek_phrase: ἐγνώσθη αὐτοῖς
chosen_rendering: was made known to them
alternate_renderings: was known to them; took notice of them
rationale: The passive Greek is striking and may imply manifestation rather than only inward awareness.

greek_phrase: ἄγγελος κυρίου
chosen_rendering: angel of the Lord
alternate_renderings: messenger of the Lord
rationale: Scene signal too strong for neutral messenger here. Direct Logos evidence stays mixed at lemma level, but this scene presents more than non-angelic courier, and project background treats the Angel of the Lord as theophanic.

greek_phrase: τί ἐστιν
chosen_rendering: what is it
alternate_renderings: here I am
rationale: The Greek here reads like a question rather than the usual readiness formula, so the draft preserves the strangeness.

greek_phrase: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν
chosen_rendering: I am the One who is
alternate_renderings: I am the Existing One; I am Being
rationale: Keeps the participial force visible without flattening it into an abstract title alone.

greek_phrase: ἐπισκοπῇ ἐπεσκέμμαι ὑμᾶς
chosen_rendering: have surely visited you
alternate_renderings: have surely attended to you; have surely looked in on you
rationale: Preserves the doubled visitation language, which carries both care and intervention.

greek_phrase: προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς
chosen_rendering: has summoned us
alternate_renderings: has called us; has called us to himself
rationale: Summoned gives the line formal force and movement without overstating intimacy.

greek_phrase: ἐὰν μὴ μετὰ χειρὸς κραταιᾶς
chosen_rendering: except under a mighty hand
alternate_renderings: unless by a mighty hand; unless compelled by a mighty hand
rationale: Keeps the image of overpowering force without adding extra words not present in the Greek.

greek_phrase: ἰσχνόφωνος καὶ βραδύγλωσσος
chosen_rendering: weak-voiced and slow-tongued
alternate_renderings: weak in speech and slow-tongued; poor speaker
rationale: Keeps the bodily and vocal imagery sharper than a generalized 'not eloquent.'

greek_phrase: δυσκώφον καὶ κωφόν
chosen_rendering: speechless and deaf
alternate_renderings: hard of hearing and deaf; mute and deaf
rationale: The Greek pair is difficult and overlapping, so the draft preserves the bodily disability language without over-resolving it.

greek_phrase: σὺ δὲ αὐτῷ ἔσῃ τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν
chosen_rendering: you will be for him in the things toward God
alternate_renderings: you will be for him in matters concerning God; you will be as God to him
rationale: This draft keeps the Greek's more oblique phrasing instead of jumping straight to a stronger interpretive paraphrase.

greek_phrase: τὰ τέρατα...ἃ ἔδωκα ἐν ταῖς χερσίν σου
chosen_rendering: gave into your hands
alternate_renderings: put in your hands; charged you with
rationale: Keeps the concrete hand-language attached to the entrusted wonders.

greek_phrase: υἱὸς πρωτότοκός μου Ἰσραήλ
chosen_rendering: Israel is my firstborn son
alternate_renderings: Israel is my firstborn; Israel my firstborn child
rationale: The explicit son-language is theologically weighty and should stay audible.

greek_phrase: ἔστη τὸ αἷμα τῆς περιτομῆς τοῦ παιδίου μου
chosen_rendering: the blood of my child's circumcision stands
alternate_renderings: the blood of my child's circumcision is staunched; here is the blood of my child's circumcision
rationale: The line is obscure, so the draft keeps the strange standing-language visible instead of smoothing it too quickly.

greek_phrase: ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεός
chosen_rendering: God had visited
alternate_renderings: God visited; God looked in on
rationale: Keeps continuity with the visitation language already used in the commission scene.

greek_phrase: οὐκ οἶδα τὸν κύριον
chosen_rendering: I do not know the Lord
alternate_renderings: I do not acknowledge the Lord; I do not recognize the Lord
rationale: Keeps Pharaoh's defiant refusal pointed and personal.

greek_phrase: λόγοις κενοῖς
chosen_rendering: empty words
alternate_renderings: vain words; empty talk
rationale: Empty words preserves Pharaoh's contempt for Moses' message without softening the insult.

greek_phrase: ἐβδελύξατε τὴν ὀσμὴν ἡμῶν
chosen_rendering: you have made our smell abhorrent
alternate_renderings: you have made our odor hateful; you have made us stink
rationale: The Greek is deliberately visceral, so the draft keeps the smell-language instead of abstracting it away.

greek_phrase: τὸ ὄνομά μου κύριος οὐκ ἐδήλωσα αὐτοῖς
chosen_rendering: my name Lord I did not make known to them
alternate_renderings: I did not reveal my name Lord to them
rationale: Preserves the tension of the Greek wording without prematurely solving the theological problem. Direct Logos export shows NETS and LES and LES2 all stay near this make-known wording rather than smoothing it away.

greek_phrase: ἐμνήσθην τῆς διαθήκης ὑμῶν
chosen_rendering: I remembered the covenant with you
alternate_renderings: I remembered your covenant; I remembered the covenant
rationale: Keeps the odd second-person Greek alive for later textual review.

greek_phrase: ἀπὸ τῆς ὀλιγοψυχίας
chosen_rendering: because of shortness of spirit
alternate_renderings: because of faint-heartedness; because of discouragement
rationale: Shortness of spirit preserves the compressed inner-life image of the Greek.

greek_phrase: ἐγὼ δὲ ἄλογός εἰμι
chosen_rendering: I am without speech
alternate_renderings: I am ineloquent; I am wordless
rationale: Keeps Moses' self-description close to the Greek rather than smoothing it into later idiom too quickly.

greek_phrase: δέδωκά σε θεὸν φαραώ
chosen_rendering: given you as god to Pharaoh
alternate_renderings: made you a god to Pharaoh; given you as divine authority to Pharaoh
rationale: Keeps the startling designation visible rather than softening it into mere representation.

greek_phrase: ἔσται δράκων
chosen_rendering: it will become a dragon
alternate_renderings: it will become a serpent
rationale: Greek uses drakon rather than the more ordinary snake-word, so the draft preserves the stronger creature term.

greek_phrase: κατίσχυσεν ἡ καρδία φαραώ
chosen_rendering: Pharaoh's heart grew strong
alternate_renderings: Pharaoh's heart prevailed; Pharaoh's heart hardened
rationale: Keeps this verb distinct from the later heavy and harden language in the plague cycle.

greek_phrase: βεβάρηται ἡ καρδία φαραώ
chosen_rendering: Pharaoh's heart has become heavy
alternate_renderings: Pharaoh's heart is weighed down; Pharaoh's heart is stubborn
rationale: Preserves the heaviness metaphor instead of flattening it into a generic stubbornness term.

greek_phrase: σκνῖφες
chosen_rendering: gnats
alternate_renderings: lice; gnats/gnats-like insects
rationale: The Greek points more naturally to a tiny flying pest than to lice, so gnats fits better.

greek_phrase: κυνομυίαν
chosen_rendering: dog-fly
alternate_renderings: fly swarm; gadfly
rationale: Keeps the specific Greek compound visible instead of replacing it with a generic swarm term.

greek_phrase: κύριος ὁ κύριος πάσης τῆς γῆς
chosen_rendering: the Lord, the Lord of all the earth
alternate_renderings: the Lord of all the earth
rationale: Retains the doubled lord-language that intensifies the claim over the whole land.

greek_phrase: δώσω διαστολήν
morphology: future active indicative 1 singular + accusative noun
chosen_rendering: I will put a distinction
alternate_renderings: I will set apart; I will make a separation
rationale: Keeps the separation language explicit in the plague contrast between Israel and Egypt.

greek_phrase: τὰ βδελύγματα τῶν αἰγυπτίων
chosen_rendering: the abominations of the Egyptians
alternate_renderings: what the Egyptians abhor; the Egyptians' abhorred things
rationale: Preserves the reciprocal offense built into the sacrifice dispute.

greek_phrase: παραδοξάσω...οὐ τελευτήσει...ῥητόν
chosen_rendering: make a wondrous distinction / not one thing
alternate_renderings: distinguish marvelously / not a word; not a thing
rationale: Keeps both the striking distinction language and the odd concluding term visible.

greek_phrase: ἕλκη φλυκτίδες ἀναζέουσαι
chosen_rendering: sores with blisters boiling up
alternate_renderings: boils with blains breaking out
rationale: Preserves the layered bodily imagery instead of compressing it into a single medical label.

greek_phrase: πάντα τὰ συναντήματά μου εἰς τὴν καρδίαν σου
chosen_rendering: all my blows into your heart
alternate_renderings: all my plagues into your heart; all my encounters into your heart
rationale: Blows keeps the force of divine strikes while retaining the inward-targeted imagery.

greek_phrase: διετηρήθης
chosen_rendering: you have been preserved
alternate_renderings: you were kept alive; you were maintained
rationale: Preserved keeps both survival and divine intentionality in view.

greek_phrase: ἔτι οὖν σὺ ἐμποιῇ
chosen_rendering: Do you still set yourself against my people
alternate_renderings: Do you still exalt yourself over my people
rationale: Keeps Pharaoh's resistant self-positioning explicit without forcing a single interpretation too narrowly.

greek_phrase: ἔδωκεν φωνὰς καὶ χάλαζαν
chosen_rendering: gave voices and hail
alternate_renderings: sent thunder and hail
rationale: Keeps the literal voice-language visible instead of immediately interpreting it as thunder.

greek_phrase: φωνὰς θεοῦ
chosen_rendering: voices of God
alternate_renderings: thunders of God
rationale: Retains the concrete voice-language in Pharaoh's plea and links it with the earlier wording.

greek_phrase: προσέθετο τοῦ ἁμαρτάνειν / ἐβάρυνεν
chosen_rendering: added to sin / made heavy
alternate_renderings: continued sinning / hardened
rationale: Keeps both the repeated sin-language and the heaviness metaphor instead of flattening them.

greek_phrase: ὅσα ἐμπέπαιχα τοῖς αἰγυπτίοις
morphology: perfect active indicative 1 singular + dative plural noun
chosen_rendering: how I mocked the Egyptians
alternate_renderings: how I made sport of the Egyptians; how I toyed with the Egyptians
rationale: Keeps the humiliation motif explicit and avoids softening the verb into mere display language.

greek_phrase: ἐντραπῆναί με
chosen_rendering: humble yourself before me
alternate_renderings: reverence me; be ashamed before me
rationale: Humble yourself fits the plague context and keeps the call to submission more clearly than a purely emotional shame reading.

greek_phrase: τὴν ἀποσκευὴν ὑμῶν / πονηρία προκεῖται ὑμῖν
morphology: accusative singular noun / nominative singular noun + present middle/passive indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: your baggage / evil lies ahead of you
alternate_renderings: your store / evil is attached to you; your belongings / harm is before you
rationale: Retains the Greek baggage-language and the ominous image of evil lying before them instead of harmonizing to the Hebrew wording.

greek_phrase: ψηλαφητὸν σκότος
chosen_rendering: darkness that can be felt
alternate_renderings: palpable darkness; touchable darkness
rationale: Keeps the bodily, tangible force of the darkness visible in the English line.

greek_phrase: σκότος γνόφος θυέλλα
chosen_rendering: darkness, gloom, storm-cloud
alternate_renderings: darkness, murk, tempest; deep darkness and storm-gloom
rationale: Preserves the piling up of overlapping darkness terms rather than collapsing them into a single adjective.

greek_phrase: ἡ ἀποσκευὴ ὑμῶν ἀποτρεχέτω μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν
morphology: nominative singular noun + present active imperative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: let your baggage go along with you
alternate_renderings: let your store depart with you; let your belongings run along with you
rationale: Keeps the odd Greek baggage wording visible instead of replacing it with children or households from another textual tradition.

greek_phrase: οὐχ ὑπολείψομεθα ὁπλήν
morphology: future active indicative 1 plural + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: we will not leave behind a hoof
alternate_renderings: we will not leave a hoof; not a hoof will remain
rationale: The idiom is already vivid in Greek and worth preserving directly.

greek_phrase: ἐκβαλεῖ ὑμᾶς ἐκβολῇ
morphology: future active indicative 3 singular + dative singular noun
chosen_rendering: he will surely drive you out with a complete expulsion
alternate_renderings: he will utterly cast you out; he will drive you out decisively
rationale: Keeps the emphatic doubled expulsion language instead of flattening it to a simple dismissal.

greek_phrase: ἐχρήσαν αὐτοῖς
chosen_rendering: they lent to them
alternate_renderings: they granted to them; they supplied them
rationale: Keeps the Greek lending language visible, even though the context may imply a broader giving or granting.

greek_phrase: ἐγὼ εἰσπορεύομαι εἰς μέσον Αἰγύπτου
morphology: present middle indicative 1 singular + prepositional phrase
chosen_rendering: I enter into the midst of Egypt
alternate_renderings: I go into Egypt's midst; I pass into the middle of Egypt
rationale: Preserves the inward movement of the Greek rather than changing it to a generic going forth.

greek_phrase: οὐ γρύξει κύων τῇ γλώσσῃ αὐτοῦ / παραδοξάσει κύριος
morphology: future active indicative 3 singular + nominative singular noun + future active indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: not a dog will snarl ... the Lord will distinguish marvelously
alternate_renderings: not a dog will move its tongue ... the Lord will make a striking distinction
rationale: Keeps both the vivid dog image and the extraordinary character of the distinction the Lord makes.

greek_phrase: ὁ λαός σου οὗ σὺ ἀφηγῇ
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + present middle indicative 2 singular
chosen_rendering: the people whom you lead
alternate_renderings: the people over whom you preside; the people you guide
rationale: Lead is clearer English while still reflecting Moses' guiding role stated in the Greek.

greek_phrase: πρόβατον
chosen_rendering: animal from the flock
alternate_renderings: lamb; sheep
rationale: Keeps the broader Greek flock-animal term visible before verse 5 narrows the acceptable source animals.

greek_phrase: σκεπάσω ὑμᾶς
chosen_rendering: I will shelter you
alternate_renderings: I will protect you; I will cover you
rationale: Preserves the covering-sheltering verb in Greek instead of replacing it with pass over language.

greek_phrase: ἐξάξω τὴν δύναμιν ὑμῶν
morphology: future active indicative 1 singular + accusative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: I will bring your hosts out
alternate_renderings: I will bring out your force; I will bring out your company
rationale: Hosts keeps the collective organized-force sense of dynamis in this exodus setting.

greek_phrase: ἐν τε τοῖς γειώραις καὶ αὐτόχθοσιν τῆς γῆς
chosen_rendering: among both the newcomer and the native-born of the land
alternate_renderings: among resident aliens and natives; among immigrants and locals
rationale: Keeps the law applying across insider-outsider lines without collapsing the social distinction.

greek_phrase: ὡς ἐσκέπασεν τοὺς οἴκους
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + accusative plural noun
chosen_rendering: who sheltered the houses
alternate_renderings: who covered the houses; who defended the houses
rationale: Matches the sheltering language already used in verse 13 and keeps the Greek verbal link visible.

greek_phrase: τῆς αἰχμαλωτίδος τῆς ἐν τῷ λάκκῳ
chosen_rendering: the captive woman in the pit
alternate_renderings: the captive maid in the dungeon; the imprisoned woman in the pit
rationale: Retains the harsher captivity-and-pit image of the Greek rather than smoothing it.

greek_phrase: ἐχρήσαν αὐτοῖς / ἐσκύλευσαν τοὺς αἰγυπτίους
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 plural / aorist active indicative 3 plural
chosen_rendering: they lent to them / they plundered the Egyptians
alternate_renderings: they granted to them / they spoiled the Egyptians
rationale: Keeps both the lending language and the stronger plunder verb side by side in the Greek sequence.

greek_phrase: ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν γῇ Χαναάν
chosen_rendering: in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan
alternate_renderings: in Egypt and Canaan
rationale: Keeps the longer textual form present in the Greek tradition, which includes Canaan in the total sojourning span.

greek_phrase: νυκτὸς προφυλακή
morphology: genitive singular noun + nominative singular noun
chosen_rendering: a night-watch kept for the Lord
alternate_renderings: a night of vigil for the Lord; a watch-night for the Lord
rationale: Preserves the vigilance-watch language rather than reducing it to a generic commemorative night.

greek_phrase: ἀργυρώνητον
chosen_rendering: one bought with silver
alternate_renderings: one purchased with money; money-bought slave
rationale: Keeps the silver-purchase wording explicit in the social-legal rule.

greek_phrase: προσήλυτος
chosen_rendering: newcomer
alternate_renderings: proselyte; resident alien; sojourner
rationale: Newcomer reads naturally while still marking someone who has attached himself to Israel from outside.

greek_phrase: νόμος εἷς
chosen_rendering: one law
alternate_renderings: single law; one rule
rationale: Keeps the emphatic unity of legal standard for native-born and newcomer alike.

greek_phrase: πρωτογενές
chosen_rendering: first issue
alternate_renderings: first produced; first offspring
rationale: Keeps the birth-origin nuance alongside firstborn instead of repeating the same English word twice.

greek_phrase: ἐν μηνὶ τῶν νέων
chosen_rendering: in the month of new grain
alternate_renderings: in the month of new things; in the month of spring growth
rationale: Preserves the Greek newness language rather than importing the later Hebrew month name.

greek_phrase: ἓξ ἡμέρας
chosen_rendering: for six days
alternate_renderings: six days
rationale: Keeps the Greek six-day wording visible, even though readers may expect seven from other textual traditions.

greek_phrase: κατὰ καιροὺς ὡρῶν ἀφ᾽ ἡμερῶν εἰς ἡμέρας
chosen_rendering: at the appointed times, from days to days
alternate_renderings: at season-times from day to day; at fixed seasons from year to year
rationale: Keeps the layered time-language instead of smoothing it immediately to annual observance.

greek_phrase: ἀσάλευτον πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου
chosen_rendering: fixed before your eyes
alternate_renderings: immovable before your eyes; steadfast before your eyes
rationale: Retains the Greek image of something set firmly before the eyes rather than importing later ritual terminology.

greek_phrase: πέμπτῃ δὲ γενεᾷ
chosen_rendering: in the fifth generation
alternate_renderings: in battle array; five in rank
rationale: Keeps the Greek genealogical wording, a notable difference from more familiar renderings.

greek_phrase: ἐν χειρὶ ὑψηλῇ
chosen_rendering: with uplifted hand
alternate_renderings: with a high hand; triumphantly
rationale: Preserves the embodied idiom without flattening it to an adverb.

greek_phrase: τὴν σωτηρίαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ
chosen_rendering: the salvation from God
alternate_renderings: the deliverance from God; the salvation of God
rationale: Keeps the explicit source phrase from God visible in the line.

greek_phrase: ἀναζευξάτωσαν
chosen_rendering: let them break camp
alternate_renderings: let them set out; let them move on
rationale: Reflects camp-movement language more concretely than a generic proceed.

greek_phrase: ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ
chosen_rendering: the angel of God
alternate_renderings: the messenger of God
rationale: Same project rule as other theophanic scenes. Figure moves with the cloud and functions as divine presence, so angel better fits than neutral messenger.

greek_phrase: ἐν ἀνέμῳ νότῳ βιαίῳ
chosen_rendering: by a violent south wind
alternate_renderings: by a strong south wind; by a violent southern wind
rationale: Preserves the Greek south-wind wording rather than harmonizing to east wind from another textual tradition.

greek_phrase: συνεδήσεν τοὺς ἄξονας
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + accusative plural noun
chosen_rendering: he bound the axles
alternate_renderings: he jammed the axles; he fastened the axles
rationale: Keeps the concrete mechanical action in the Greek account.

greek_phrase: ἐξετίναξεν κύριος τοὺς αἰγυπτίους
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + accusative plural noun
chosen_rendering: the Lord shook the Egyptians off
alternate_renderings: the Lord cast off the Egyptians; the Lord flung the Egyptians away
rationale: Preserves the vivid shaking-off image of the Greek.

greek_phrase: Μωϋσῇ τῷ θεράποντι αὐτοῦ
chosen_rendering: Moses his attendant
alternate_renderings: Moses his servant; Moses his minister
rationale: Keeps therapon distinct from the more common slave-servant wording and suggests honored service.

greek_phrase: ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται
chosen_rendering: he has been glorified gloriously
alternate_renderings: he is greatly glorified; he has glorified himself gloriously
rationale: Keeps the doubled glory-language of the Greek song rather than reducing it to a single intensifier.

greek_phrase: βοηθὸς καὶ σκεπαστὴς
chosen_rendering: helper and shelter
alternate_renderings: helper and protector; helper and coverer
rationale: Preserves the paired rescue nouns and keeps the shelter motif visible.

greek_phrase: κύριος συντρίβων πολέμους
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + present active participle
chosen_rendering: The Lord shattering wars
alternate_renderings: The Lord breaking wars; the Lord bringing wars to nothing
rationale: Greek here speaks of God crushing wars, a notable difference from the more familiar man-of-war wording.

greek_phrase: δια πνεύματος τοῦ θυμοῦ σου / ἐπάγη
morphology: genitive singular noun phrase / aorist passive indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: by the breath of your wrath ... congealed
alternate_renderings: by the wind of your fury ... froze; by the blast of your anger ... stiffened
rationale: Keeps both the bodily wrath-breath image and the congealing language of the sea.

greek_phrase: ἀπέστειλας τὸ πνεῦμά σου
morphology: aorist active indicative 2 singular + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: You sent out your wind
alternate_renderings: You sent out your spirit; You sent out your breath
rationale: In context the sea-response favors wind, while still echoing the earlier breath imagery.

greek_phrase: παρεκάλεσας τῇ ἰσχύι σου εἰς κατάλυμα ἅγιόν σου
morphology: aorist active indicative 2 singular + dative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: by your strength you led them onward to your holy resting-place
alternate_renderings: you comforted them into your holy lodging-place; you called them to your holy resting-place
rationale: Aims to keep the movement toward holy lodging-rest without flattening the unusual verb.

greek_phrase: ὤργισθησαν
chosen_rendering: grew angry
alternate_renderings: were enraged; were disturbed
rationale: Greek says the nations became angry, a sharper reaction than simple fear.

greek_phrase: ἀπολιθωθήτωσαν
chosen_rendering: let them turn to stone
alternate_renderings: let them become stone; let them be petrified
rationale: Keeps the stone-image directly in the English line.

greek_phrase: τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ ἐπ᾽ αἰῶνα καὶ ἔτι
chosen_rendering: forever and beyond
alternate_renderings: forever and ever and still; for the age and beyond the age
rationale: Preserves the piling-up of endless duration without wooden repetition.

greek_phrase: ξύλον ... ἔθετο αὐτῷ ... ἐπείρασεν αὐτόν
morphology: accusative singular noun / aorist active indicative 3 singular / aorist active indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: a piece of wood ... he set for him ... he tested him
alternate_renderings: wood ... set for them ... tested them
rationale: Keeps both the wood-image and the singular pronouns, which may treat Israel as a collective singular.

greek_phrase: ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι κύριος ὁ ἰώμενός σε
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + present middle participle
chosen_rendering: I am the Lord who heals you
alternate_renderings: I am the Lord your healer; I am the Lord healing you
rationale: Keeps the divine self-identification in direct healing language.

greek_phrase: ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ὕω ὑμῖν ἄρτους
morphology: present active indicative 1 singular + accusative plural noun
chosen_rendering: I am raining bread for you
alternate_renderings: I will rain bread for you; I rain loaves for you
rationale: Keeps the weather-verb vivid in the present line of divine action.

greek_phrase: ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ
chosen_rendering: against God
alternate_renderings: before God; toward God
rationale: Keeps the text explicitly naming God rather than shifting to Lord in this accusation line.

greek_phrase: γόμορ
chosen_rendering: gomor
alternate_renderings: omer; homer
rationale: Keeps the Greek measure-form visible instead of normalizing to another traditional form.

greek_phrase: ἐπικράνθη
chosen_rendering: Moses was embittered against them
alternate_renderings: Moses was angered with them; Moses was made bitter toward them
rationale: Preserves the bitterness-language rather than flattening it to generic irritation.

greek_phrase: σάββατα ἀνάπαυσις ἁγία
chosen_rendering: Sabbath, a holy rest
alternate_renderings: sabbaths, holy resting; sabbath-rest holy
rationale: Captures the sabbath-rest wording in readable English while preserving the holy-rest emphasis.

greek_phrase: ἐσαββάτισεν
chosen_rendering: the people Sabbathed
alternate_renderings: the people kept sabbath; the people rested sabbath
rationale: Keeps the verbal sabbath form explicit instead of paraphrasing away the wordplay.

greek_phrase: μάν
chosen_rendering: Man
alternate_renderings: Manna
rationale: Keeps the Greek form of the name visible in this draft tradition.

greek_phrase: εἰς μέρος τῆς Φοινίκης
chosen_rendering: to the region of Phoenicia
alternate_renderings: to the part of Phoenicia; to Phoenicia's border-region
rationale: Preserves the striking Greek geographical wording rather than harmonizing it away.

greek_phrase: τὸ δέκατον τῶν τριῶν μέτρων
chosen_rendering: the tenth part of three measures
alternate_renderings: one tenth of three measures
rationale: Keeps the Greek explanatory measure note directly visible.

greek_phrase: ἐλοιδορεῖτο ... τί λοιδορεῖσθέ μοι
morphology: imperfect middle/passive indicative 3 singular / present middle-passive indicative 2 plural
chosen_rendering: reviled / revile
alternate_renderings: quarreled with; abused; reproached
rationale: Keeps the sharper insult-language of the Greek rather than softening it to mere dispute.

greek_phrase: ὅδε ἐγὼ ἕστηκα
chosen_rendering: I am standing
alternate_renderings: Here I stand; I have stood
rationale: Preserves the vivid immediacy of the divine stance at the rock. Current wording stays close to source-row Greek.

greek_phrase: πειρασμός καὶ λοιδόρησις
chosen_rendering: Testing and Reviling
alternate_renderings: Temptation and Reviling; Trial and Abuse
rationale: Keeps both place-name nouns tied directly to the people's actions against Moses and the Lord.

greek_phrase: παράταξαι
chosen_rendering: draw up in battle array
alternate_renderings: set in array; line up for battle
rationale: Keeps the military formation sense instead of generic fight wording. Current line stays close to source-row Greek.

greek_phrase: ἐτρέψατο
chosen_rendering: routed
alternate_renderings: turned back; put to flight
rationale: Routed expresses the defeat implied by the battle-turning verb in context.

greek_phrase: ἀλοίφῃ ἐξαλείψω
morphology: dative/infinitive-like emphatic expression + future active indicative 1 singular
chosen_rendering: in wiping out I will wipe out
alternate_renderings: I will utterly blot out; blotting out I will blot out
rationale: Keeps the emphatic doubled erasure language visible.

greek_phrase: κύριος μου καταφυγή
chosen_rendering: The Lord is my refuge
alternate_renderings: The Lord my refuge; The Lord my shelter
rationale: Makes the altar-name read clearly while preserving the refuge motif.

greek_phrase: ἐν χειρὶ κρυφαίᾳ
chosen_rendering: with hidden hand
alternate_renderings: with secret hand; by concealed hand
rationale: Keeps the strange and important Greek image instead of normalizing it away.

greek_phrase: μετὰ τὴν ἄφεσιν αὐτῆς
chosen_rendering: after her sending away
alternate_renderings: after her release; after he had sent her away
rationale: Keeps the Greek dismissal/release wording visible without over-deciding the precise marital or logistical nuance.

greek_phrase: ἐνεκεν τούτου ὅτι ἐπέθεντο αὐτοῖς
morphology: causal phrase + aorist middle indicative 3 plural
chosen_rendering: because in this matter they acted arrogantly against them
alternate_renderings: because they attacked them in this matter; because they dealt proudly against them
rationale: Preserves the morally charged overreaching sense rather than reducing the line to simple hostility.

greek_phrase: φθορᾷ καταφθαρήσῃ ἀνυπομονήτῳ
morphology: dative singular noun + future middle/passive indicative 2 singular + dative singular adjective
chosen_rendering: With ruin you will wear away, with exhaustion unbearable
alternate_renderings: You will utterly wear out with intolerable strain; you will be ruined with unbearable exhaustion
rationale: Keeps the doubled wear-ruin emphasis and the strong adjective rather than flattening it to simple tiredness.

greek_phrase: γίνου σὺ τῷ λαῷ τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν
morphology: present middle imperative 2 singular + neuter plural phrase
chosen_rendering: Be for the people in the things toward God
alternate_renderings: Be the people's representative before God; be for the people in matters pertaining to God
rationale: Keeps the slightly awkward but important relational phrasing of the Greek instead of over-interpreting it.

greek_phrase: μισοῦντας ὑπερηφανίαν
morphology: present active participle accusative plural + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: hating arrogance
alternate_renderings: hating pride; hating overbearing conduct
rationale: Arrogance captures the social and moral edge of the Greek better than a flatter abstract pride.

greek_phrase: τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ ὑπέρογκον
chosen_rendering: the over-large matter
alternate_renderings: the overburdensome matter; the weighty matter; the too great matter
rationale: Keeps the sense of something swollen beyond ordinary scale, not merely big in importance.

greek_phrase: κατισχύσει σε ὁ θεός καὶ δυνήσῃ παραστῆναι
morphology: future active indicative 3 singular + future middle indicative 2 singular + aorist active infinitive
chosen_rendering: God will strengthen you, and you will be able to stand
alternate_renderings: God will sustain you, and you will endure; God will prevail for you, and you will be able to remain
rationale: Reads the cluster as divine strengthening leading to Moses' endurance in office.

greek_phrase: λαὸς περιούσιος
chosen_rendering: a people of special possession
alternate_renderings: a peculiar people; a treasured people; a possession people
rationale: Keeps the possession-belonging nuance of the Greek without using the now-misleading English peculiar.

greek_phrase: βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα
chosen_rendering: a royal priesthood
alternate_renderings: a kingly priesthood; a kingdom of priests
rationale: Royal priesthood reads naturally and stays close to the Greek form used here.

greek_phrase: ποιήσομεν καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα
chosen_rendering: we will do and we will hear
alternate_renderings: we will do and obey; we will act and listen
rationale: Preserves the Greek order instead of resolving hearing into interpretation too early.

greek_phrase: ἐν στύλῳ νεφέλης
chosen_rendering: in a pillar of cloud
alternate_renderings: in a cloud-pillar
rationale: Keeps the familiar theophanic image directly from the Greek wording.

greek_phrase: ὅταν αἱ φωναὶ καὶ αἱ σάλπιγγες καὶ ἡ νεφέλη ἀπέλθῃ
morphology: temporal clause with plural/singular subject chain
chosen_rendering: When the voices and the trumpets and the cloud depart from the mountain
alternate_renderings: When the thunderings and trumpets and cloud withdraw; when the sounds and trumpets and cloud move away
rationale: Keeps the difficult Greek departure condition visible rather than harmonizing it away.

greek_phrase: νεφέλη γνοφώδης
chosen_rendering: a gloomy cloud
alternate_renderings: a dark cloud; a murky cloud
rationale: Tries to preserve the thick, ominous quality of the Greek modifier.

greek_phrase: καταβεβηκέναι ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸ τὸν θεόν
morphology: perfect active infinitive + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: because God had come down upon it
alternate_renderings: because God had descended upon it; because the divine one had come down on it
rationale: Keeps the Greek subject as God in this line, matching the text as given.

greek_phrase: κατανοῆσαι
chosen_rendering: to gaze
alternate_renderings: to look closely; to inspect; to peer
rationale: Conveys dangerous looking-through or scrutinizing without making it merely visual glance.

greek_phrase: μήποτε ἀπαλλάξῃ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν κύριος
chosen_rendering: lest the Lord break out against some of them
alternate_renderings: lest the Lord separate some from them; lest the Lord remove some of them
rationale: Context favors a punitive outbreak, though the Greek verb remains unusual enough to note.

greek_phrase: μὴ βιαζέσθωσαν
chosen_rendering: let them not force their way
alternate_renderings: let them not press in; let them not break through
rationale: Keeps the forceful breach imagery of the warning.

greek_phrase: ἀποδιδούς ἁμαρτίας πατέρων ἐπὶ τέκνα
morphology: present active participle + accusative plural noun phrase
chosen_rendering: repaying fathers' sins upon children
alternate_renderings: visiting fathers' sins on children; rendering back fathers' iniquities upon children
rationale: Keeps the strong repayment language of the Greek rather than softening it to mere consequence.

greek_phrase: ἐπὶ ματαίῳ
chosen_rendering: in vain
alternate_renderings: upon emptiness; for vanity; for what is empty
rationale: English witness tradition is unanimous here, and in vain remains a faithful idiomatic rendering of the Greek phrase while the footnote preserves the emptiness/vanity nuance.

greek_phrase: τὴν ἡμέραν τῶν σαββάτων
morphology: accusative singular noun phrase + genitive plural noun
chosen_rendering: the day of the Sabbaths
alternate_renderings: the sabbath day; the day of sabbath-rests
rationale: Keeps the plural sabbath wording visible in the Greek.

greek_phrase: οὐ μοιχεύσεις / οὐ κλέψεις / οὐ φονεύσεις
chosen_rendering: You shall not commit adultery / steal / murder
alternate_renderings: You shall not adulterate marriage / steal / kill
rationale: Preserves the Greek command order, which differs from the order many readers expect in English tradition.

greek_phrase: μαρτυρίαν ψευδῆ
chosen_rendering: false testimony
alternate_renderings: a lying witness; false witness
rationale: Keeps the explicit testimony noun visible at the end of the line.

greek_phrase: ἐώρα τὴν φωνήν
morphology: imperfect active indicative 3 plural + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: were seeing the voice
alternate_renderings: perceived the sound; saw the thunderings
rationale: Preserves the striking sensory overlap in the Greek instead of resolving it into a safer paraphrase.

greek_phrase: ἕνεκεν γὰρ τοῦ πειράσαι ὑμᾶς
chosen_rendering: for the sake of testing you
alternate_renderings: to test you; on account of testing you
rationale: Keeps the explicit purpose phrasing of the theophany.

greek_phrase: εἰς τὸν γνόφον
chosen_rendering: into the gloom
alternate_renderings: into the darkness; into the thick darkness
rationale: Aims to preserve the dense, ominous darkness term without flattening it.

greek_phrase: τὰ σωτήρια ὑμῶν
chosen_rendering: your offerings of salvation
alternate_renderings: your peace-offerings; your offerings of deliverance; your well-being offerings
rationale: Keeps the salvation-shaped Greek noun visible rather than simply importing a traditional cultic label. Direct Logos export confirms NETS stays salvation-shaped while LES and LES2 smooth to peace-offerings.

greek_phrase: οὗ ἐὰν ἐπονομάσω τὸ ὄνομά μου
morphology: relative clause + aorist active subjunctive 1 singular
chosen_rendering: where I cause my name to be called
alternate_renderings: where I name my name; where I record my name; where I cause my name to be invoked
rationale: Brings the clause into line with the project's broader name-formula handling while still keeping the Greek naming idiom visible. Direct Logos export confirms NETS stays closer to name-called wording while LES and LES2 smooth toward place-my-name phrasing.

greek_phrase: μεμίανται
chosen_rendering: they have been defiled
alternate_renderings: they are profaned; they stand polluted
rationale: Keeps the ritual defilement result explicit once the tool touches the stones.

greek_phrase: πρὸς τὸ κριτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ
chosen_rendering: the judgment-seat of God
alternate_renderings: before God; to God's court
rationale: Keeps the legal forum language explicit instead of flattening the scene into a vague religious appearance.

greek_phrase: ἠθέτησεν ἐν αὐτῇ
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + prepositional phrase
chosen_rendering: he has broken faith with her
alternate_renderings: he has dealt faithlessly with her; he has trifled with her
rationale: Preserves covenantal betrayal force in the verb rather than making the offense merely emotional.

greek_phrase: δύο καὶ εἴκοσι χιλιάδες

greek_phrase: ἀπὸ εἴκοσι καὶ πέντε ἐτῶν
chosen_rendering: from twenty-five years old and upward
alternate_renderings: from age twenty-five upward

greek_phrase: οὐχ ἅψονται τῶν ἁγίων ἵνα μὴ ἀποθάνωσιν

chosen_rendering: they shall not touch the holy things, lest they die

greek_phrase: ἰδεῖν ἐξάπινα τὰ ἅγια

chosen_rendering: to look suddenly upon the holy things
alternate_renderings: to look in on the holy things in an instant

greek_phrase: τὸ ὕδωρ τοῦ ἐλεγμοῦ τοῦ ἐπικαταρωμένου
chosen_rendering: the water of reproof, this cursed water
alternate_renderings: the water of conviction, the accursed water

greek_phrase: τὸν μηρόν σου διαπεπτωκότα
morphology: accusative singular noun + perfect active participle
chosen_rendering: your thigh fallen away
alternate_renderings: your thigh wasting away
rationale: Keeps the striking bodily judgment wording visible in this oath formula.

greek_phrase: μεγάλως εὔξηται εὐχήν ἀφαγνίσασθαι ἁγνείαν

chosen_rendering: greatly vows a vow, to consecrate a consecration
alternate_renderings: makes a special vow of consecration

greek_phrase: τρέφων κόμην τρίχα κεφαλῆς
morphology: present active participle + accusative noun phrase
chosen_rendering: letting the hair of his head grow long
alternate_renderings: nourishing the locks of his head

greek_phrase: ἥμαρτεν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + preposition phrase
chosen_rendering: he sinned concerning the dead person
alternate_renderings: he sinned because of the corpse

greek_phrase: οὕτως εὐλογήσετε
chosen_rendering: Thus you shall bless
alternate_renderings: In this way you shall bless

greek_phrase: ἓξ ἁμάξας λαμπηνικάς
chosen_rendering: six covered wagons
alternate_renderings: six transport wagons
rationale: Uses a practical transport term while retaining the distinct wagon gift in the dedication scene.

greek_phrase: ἄρχων εἷς καθ᾽ ἡμέραν
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + distributive prepositional phrase
chosen_rendering: One chief each day
alternate_renderings: one ruler per day

greek_phrase: οὗτος ὁ ἐγκαινισμὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + genitive singular noun
chosen_rendering: This was the dedication of the altar
alternate_renderings: this was the inauguration of the altar
rationale: Keeps the formal dedication language at the chapter summary.

greek_phrase: ἤκουσεν τὴν φωνὴν Κυρίου λαλοῦντος
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + accusative singular noun phrase + present active participle
chosen_rendering: he heard the voice of the Lord speaking
alternate_renderings: he heard the voice speaking

greek_phrase: ἀφοριεῖ ... ἀπόδομα
morphology: future active indicative 3 singular + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: set apart ... as an offering
alternate_renderings: present as a set-apart gift
rationale: Keeps both the separation and offering sense in the Levites' dedication.

greek_phrase: ἀπόδομα ἀποδεδομένοι
morphology: nominative singular noun + perfect passive participle plural
chosen_rendering: given as a gift, gift-given
alternate_renderings: wholly given over
rationale: Leaves the emphatic doubled gift-language visible rather than flattening it immediately.

greek_phrase: ἐξολεθρευθήσεται ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκείνη
morphology: future passive indicative 3 singular + nominative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: that soul shall be cut off
alternate_renderings: that person shall be destroyed
rationale: Keeps the covenant-cutting formula plain and recognizable.

greek_phrase: ἡ νεφέλη ... ὡς εἶδος πυρός
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + comparative phrase
chosen_rendering: the cloud ... like the appearance of fire
alternate_renderings: the cloud ... as a sight of fire
rationale: Preserves the paired cloud-and-fire guidance image at the tent.

greek_phrase: δύο σάλπιγγας ἀργυρᾶς ἐλατάς
chosen_rendering: two hammered silver trumpets
alternate_renderings: two beaten silver trumpets
rationale: Keeps both the material and crafted form of the signal instruments.

greek_phrase: τῷ γαμβρῷ Μωυσῆ
chosen_rendering: Moses' relative by marriage
alternate_renderings: Moses' father-in-law; Moses' brother-in-law
rationale: Leaves the kinship term open where the Greek can point to more than one in-law relation.

greek_phrase: κατασκέψασθαι αὐτοῖς ἀνάπαυσιν
morphology: aorist middle infinitive + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: to seek out rest for them
alternate_renderings: to find a resting place for them
rationale: Keeps the ark actively going before them to search out their resting place.

greek_phrase: ὁ ἐπίμικτος ... ἐπεθύμησαν ἐπιθυμίαν
chosen_rendering: the mixed company ... desired a desire
alternate_renderings: the mixed multitude ... craved intensely
rationale: Preserves both the mixed-group label and the emphatic cognate desire phrasing.

greek_phrase: ἀφελῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπὶ σοί
morphology: future active indicative 1 singular + genitive singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: I will take from the Spirit upon you
alternate_renderings: I will take some of the spirit on you
rationale: Keeps the transfer of Spirit-language explicit in the appointment of the seventy elders.

greek_phrase: ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθῃ ἐκ τῶν μυκτήρων ὑμῶν
morphology: conjunction + aorist subjunctive 3 singular + genitive plural noun
chosen_rendering: until it comes out of your nostrils
alternate_renderings: until it comes out your nose
rationale: Keeps the deliberately harsh bodily image in the judgment speech.

greek_phrase: τίς δῴη πάντα τὸν λαὸν Κυρίου προφήτας
chosen_rendering: Would that all the Lord's people were prophets
alternate_renderings: Who will give that all the Lord's people be prophets?
rationale: Keeps Moses' striking wish in a natural English optative form.

greek_phrase: τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς Αἰθιοπίσσης
chosen_rendering: the Cushite woman
alternate_renderings: the Ethiopian woman
rationale: Uses a broader ancient-ethnic rendering while staying close to the Greek term.

greek_phrase: στόμα κατὰ στόμα
chosen_rendering: mouth to mouth
alternate_renderings: face to face; directly
rationale: Keeps the striking directness formula in the Lord's defense of Moses.

greek_phrase: ἐπωνόμασεν ... Ἰησοῦν
morphology: aorist active indicative 3 singular + accusative singular proper noun
chosen_rendering: renamed ... Joshua
alternate_renderings: renamed ... Iesous/Jesus
rationale: Uses the familiar English form Joshua while noting the Greek name form behind it.

greek_phrase: γῆ κατεσθούσα τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + present active participle phrase
chosen_rendering: a land devouring those dwelling upon it
alternate_renderings: a land that eats its inhabitants
rationale: Keeps the exaggerated, ominous image in the spies' bad report.

greek_phrase: κατάβρωμα ἡμῖν ἐστιν
chosen_rendering: they are food for us
alternate_renderings: they are prey for us
rationale: Keeps the stark consumption image in Joshua and Caleb's confidence speech.

greek_phrase: καθαρισμῷ οὐ καθαριεῖ τὸν ἔνοχον
morphology: dative singular noun + future active indicative + accusative singular adjective
chosen_rendering: in cleansing will not cleanse the guilty
alternate_renderings: though cleansing, he will not clear the guilty
rationale: Keeps the emphatic doubled cleansing formula visible in the mercy-judgment confession.

greek_phrase: ἐν χειρὶ ὑπερηφανίας
chosen_rendering: with a hand of arrogance
alternate_renderings: with a high hand
rationale: Keeps the proud-defiant force of the idiom while remaining readable in English.

greek_phrase: κρασπέδα ... κλῶσμα ὑακίνθινον
morphology: accusative plural noun + accusative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: tassels ... a blue cord
alternate_renderings: fringes ... a blue thread
rationale: Uses natural garment-language while preserving the distinctive blue element.

greek_phrase: πᾶσα ἡ συναγωγή πάντες ἅγιοι
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + nominative plural adjective
chosen_rendering: the whole congregation, every one of them, is holy
alternate_renderings: all the congregation are holy, every one of them
rationale: Keeps the democratic holiness claim explicit in Korah's challenge.

greek_phrase: θεὸς θεὸς τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ πάσης σαρκός
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + genitive plural/singular nouns
chosen_rendering: God, God of the spirits and of all flesh
alternate_renderings: God of the spirits of all flesh
rationale: Preserves the solemn doubled divine address in Moses' intercession.

greek_phrase: καταβήσονται ζῶντες εἰς Ἅδου
morphology: future middle indicative 3 plural + nominative plural participle + preposition phrase
chosen_rendering: they go down alive into Hades
alternate_renderings: they descend alive into the grave/underworld
rationale: Keeps the Greek underworld term visible in this judgment sign.

greek_phrase: ἐβλάστησεν ... ἐξήνεγκεν βλαστόν ... ἐξήνθησεν ἄνθη ... ἐβλάστησεν κάρυα
chosen_rendering: had sprouted and brought forth a shoot and bloomed blossoms and sprouted nuts
alternate_renderings: had budded, blossomed, and borne almonds
rationale: Keeps the full staged sequence of Aaron's rod coming to life in one night.

greek_phrase: διαθήκη ἁλὸς αἰωνίου
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + genitive singular noun
chosen_rendering: a covenant of everlasting salt
alternate_renderings: an eternal covenant of salt
rationale: Keeps the unusual covenant phrase visible instead of flattening it into a generic lasting agreement. Existing English witnesses stay close enough to keep the covenant-of-salt wording.

greek_phrase: ἐγὼ μερίς σου καὶ κληρονομία σου
morphology: nominative singular pronoun + nominative singular nouns
chosen_rendering: I am your part and your inheritance
alternate_renderings: I am your portion and your inheritance
rationale: Preserves the direct divine self-identification as Aaron's share among Israel.

greek_phrase: δάμαλιν πυρρὰν ἄμωμον
chosen_rendering: a red heifer, unblemished
alternate_renderings: a reddish cow without blemish
rationale: Uses the established animal term while keeping the color and sacrificial condition explicit.

greek_phrase: τὴν σκηνὴν Κυρίου ἐμίανεν
morphology: accusative singular noun phrase + aorist active indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: has defiled the tent of the Lord
alternate_renderings: has polluted the Lord's tabernacle
rationale: Keeps the impurity offense tied directly to the sanctuary, not only to the person.

greek_phrase: ὕδωρ ἀντιλογίας ... ἡγιάσθη ἐν αὐτοῖς
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + aorist passive indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: water of reviling ... he was sanctified among them
alternate_renderings: water of contradiction / contention
rationale: Keeps the naming tied both to Israels complaint and to the Lords self-sanctifying response.

greek_phrase: προστεθήτω Ἀαρὼν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ
morphology: aorist passive imperative 3 singular + accusative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: Let Aaron be added to his people
alternate_renderings: Let Aaron be gathered to his people
rationale: Keeps the Greek added-to-his-people formula instead of replacing it with a smoother burial euphemism.

greek_phrase: ὁ ἄρτος ὁ διάκενος
chosen_rendering: this empty bread
alternate_renderings: this worthless bread
rationale: Preserves the insult in the peoples complaint without smoothing it into an interpretive paraphrase.

greek_phrase: θὲς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ σημείου
morphology: aorist active imperative 2 singular + preposition phrase
chosen_rendering: set it on a sign
alternate_renderings: set it on a standard / sign-pole
rationale: Leaves the Greek sign-language visible before later traditions specify how the lifted serpent should be imagined.

greek_phrase: ἐν βιβλίῳ Πόλεμος τοῦ Κυρίου
chosen_rendering: in the Book, The War of the Lord
alternate_renderings: in the Book of the War of the Lord
rationale: Keeps the citation formula rough and visible, since the line appears to quote a named source or heading.

greek_phrase: ἀνέστη ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνδιαβαλεῖν αὐτόν
chosen_rendering: the angel of God rose up to oppose him
alternate_renderings: to stand against / accuse him
rationale: Hostile blocking sense still matters, but figure should not stay neutral messenger. Scene presents angelic divine opponent with drawn sword and worship response later in context.

greek_phrase: οὐχ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ὁ θεὸς διαρτηθῆναι
chosen_rendering: God is not like a man, to waver
alternate_renderings: to be unsettled / thrown off balance
rationale: Keeps the contrast pointed at divine constancy even though the Greek verb is unusual and needs later review.

greek_phrase: ὡς δόξα μονοκέρωτος
chosen_rendering: like the glory of a one-horned beast
alternate_renderings: like the strength/glory of a unicorn
rationale: Preserves the strange Greek creature term instead of replacing it with a fully harmonized animal guess.

greek_phrase: ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον ἐξ Ἰακώβ
morphology: future active indicative 3 singular + nominative singular noun
chosen_rendering: A star shall rise out of Jacob
alternate_renderings: A star shall come up from Jacob
rationale: Keeps the astral royal image explicit and separate from the following man-from-Israel line.

greek_phrase: κακώσουσιν Ἐβραίους
morphology: future active indicative 3 plural + accusative plural noun
chosen_rendering: they shall afflict Hebrews
alternate_renderings: they shall afflict the Hebrews
rationale: Keeps the explicit ethnic label Hebrews instead of smoothing it into a generic Israel reference.

greek_phrase: ἐν τῷ ζηλῶσαί μου τὸν ζῆλον ἐν αὐτοῖς
chosen_rendering: by being jealous with my jealousy among them
alternate_renderings: by zealing my zeal among them
rationale: Keeps the doubled zeal wording visible instead of flattening Phinehas into a generic defender of honor.

greek_phrase: διαθήκη ἱερατείας αἰωνία
chosen_rendering: a covenant of everlasting priesthood
alternate_renderings: an eternal priestly covenant
rationale: Preserves both covenant language and the priesthood focus without smoothing the phrase into abstract office language.

greek_phrase: ὀρθῶς ... λελαλήκασιν
chosen_rendering: have spoken rightly
alternate_renderings: have spoken correctly
rationale: Keeps the divine approval of the daughters argument explicit before the inheritance ruling is stated.

greek_phrase: ὁ θεὸς τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ πάσης σαρκός
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + genitive plural/singular nouns
chosen_rendering: the God of the spirits and of all flesh
alternate_renderings: God of the spirits of all flesh
rationale: Matches the same solemn formula used earlier in Numbers and keeps the universal scope visible.

greek_phrase: ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἔχει πνεῦμα ἐν ἑαυτῷ
chosen_rendering: a man who has spirit in himself
alternate_renderings: a man in whom there is spirit
rationale: Keeps the inward spirit-language direct instead of turning the line into a later doctrinal formula.

greek_phrase: τὴν κρίσιν τῶν δήλων
morphology: accusative singular noun phrase + genitive plural adjective used substantively
chosen_rendering: the judgment of the Disclosures
alternate_renderings: the judgment of the Manifestations; the judgment of the clear tokens / Urim-like disclosures
rationale: Tracks the same disclosure vocabulary already used in Exodus for the Greek rendering behind the later English Urim and Thummim language instead of importing a fixed transliteration without signal.

greek_phrase: ἡμέρα σημασίας ἔσται ὑμῖν
chosen_rendering: It shall be a day of signal for you
alternate_renderings: a day of signaling / trumpet signal
rationale: Keeps the Greek signal-language visible without forcing a later liturgical label into the line.

greek_phrase: ἐξόδιον ἔσται ὑμῖν
chosen_rendering: there shall be a dismissal for you
alternate_renderings: a closing assembly / departure day
rationale: Leaves the closing-dismissal sense exposed instead of harmonizing it immediately with later feast terminology.

greek_phrase: οὐ βεβηλώσει τὸ ῥῆμα αὐτοῦ
morphology: future active indicative 3 singular + accusative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: he shall not profane his word
alternate_renderings: he shall not treat his word as common
rationale: Keeps vow-breaking in the Greek category of profanation, not merely failure to perform.

greek_phrase: ὅρκος δεσμοῦ κακῶσαι ψυχήν
chosen_rendering: Every vow and every binding oath to afflict a life
alternate_renderings: to afflict the soul
rationale: Keeps the Greek life/soul wording available instead of pre-deciding the phrase in one devotional direction.

greek_phrase: ἐκδίκει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν ... καὶ ἔσχατον προστεθήσῃ
morphology: present imperative + accusative noun + future passive indicative
chosen_rendering: Avenge the vengeance ... and at the end you shall be added to your people
alternate_renderings: Take vengeance ... then be gathered to your people
rationale: Keeps the doubled vengeance wording and the death formula together in the same commission.

greek_phrase: κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμα Βαλαάμ τοῦ ἀποστῆσαι
chosen_rendering: according to the word of Balaam, a cause to depart
alternate_renderings: by Balaams counsel, to turn away
rationale: Preserves Balaams word as the named source of Israels turning aside.

greek_phrase: γνώσεσθε τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ὑμῶν ὅταν ὑμᾶς καταλάβῃ τὰ κακά
morphology: future middle indicative + accusative noun phrase + temporal clause
chosen_rendering: you shall know your sin when evils overtake you
alternate_renderings: you will know your sin when disaster catches you
rationale: Keeps the warning tied to sin becoming known through overtaking evils, not only through abstract guilt.

greek_phrase: σκόλοπες ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ... βολίδες ἐν ταῖς πλευραῖς
chosen_rendering: spikes in your eyes and darts in your sides
alternate_renderings: thorns in your eyes and missiles in your flanks
rationale: Retains the two sharp bodily images rather than collapsing them into one generic trouble phrase.

greek_phrase: τὰς ἓξ πόλεις τῶν φυγαδευτηρίων
chosen_rendering: the six cities of refuges
alternate_renderings: the six refuge cities
rationale: Keeps the flight/refuge sense explicit in the Greek compound instead of reducing it to a simple city label.

greek_phrase: ἕως ἂν ἀποθάνῃ ὁ ἱερεὺς ὁ μέγας
morphology: temporal clause + nominative singular noun phrase
chosen_rendering: until the great priest dies
alternate_renderings: until the high priest dies
rationale: Leaves the title in its direct Greek form while preserving the release marker tied to that death.

greek_phrase: τὸ αἷμα τοῦτο φονοκτονεῖ τὴν γῆν
morphology: nominative singular noun phrase + present active indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: blood murders the land
alternate_renderings: blood blood-guilts the land
rationale: Keeps the verbal shock of the Greek by making blood itself the active polluting murderer of the land.

greek_phrase: οὐχὶ περιστραφήσεται κληρονομία ... ἀπὸ φυλῆς ἐπὶ φυλήν
morphology: future passive indicative 3 singular + preposition phrase
chosen_rendering: inheritance shall not be turned around ... from tribe to tribe
alternate_renderings: shall not be transferred / turned aside
rationale: Keeps the rotational movement image in the Greek rather than flattening it into a bare legal transfer term.

greek_phrase: ὡς εἴ τις τροφοφορήσει ἄνθρωπος τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ
morphology: comparative clause + future active indicative 3 singular
chosen_rendering: as someone would carry his son
alternate_renderings: as a man nourishes/carries his son
rationale: Keeps the parental carrying image direct instead of shifting immediately to a generalized care metaphor.

greek_phrase: ὡς εἰ ποιήσαισαν αἱ μέλισσαι
chosen_rendering: as bees might do
alternate_renderings: like bees act/swarm
rationale: Preserves the stinging swarm image without softening the pursuit into a generic chase.

greek_phrase: οὐκ ἐπεδεήθης ῥήματος
morphology: aorist passive indicative 2 singular + genitive singular noun
chosen_rendering: You lacked no thing
alternate_renderings: You were in need of no word/thing
rationale: Keeps the line terse and absolute, reflecting the Greek without over-specifying the object of lack.

greek_phrase: ὠδῖνας ἕξουσιν ἀπὸ προσώπου σου
morphology: accusative plural noun + future active indicative 3 plural
chosen_rendering: shall have birth-pains from before your face
alternate_renderings: shall writhe in pangs before you
rationale: Keeps the labor-pain image explicit in the terror promised among the nations.

greek_phrase: ἐσκλήρυνεν ... τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ καὶ κατίσχυσεν τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ
chosen_rendering: hardened his spirit and strengthened his heart
alternate_renderings: made his spirit stubborn and his heart strong
rationale: Preserves the paired inner terms spirit and heart instead of collapsing the hardening to one flat formula. Brenton stays close enough to support keeping the paired wording.

greek_phrase: τίς θεὸς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὅστις ποιήσει καθὰ πεποίηκας
chosen_rendering: what god is there in heaven or on earth who will do as you did
alternate_renderings: what god exists...; who can do as you have done
rationale: Keeps Moses rhetorical comparison direct and open, without smoothing the challenge into abstract uniqueness language.

greek_phrase: τὰ δέκα ῥήματα
chosen_rendering: the ten words
alternate_renderings: the ten commandments; the ten sayings
rationale: Preserves the Greek expression itself rather than substituting the later conventional label commandments.

greek_phrase: πῦρ καταναλίσκον, θεὸς ζηλωτής
chosen_rendering: a consuming fire, a jealous God
alternate_renderings: fire that consumes; zealous God
rationale: Keeps the stark double predicate intact because both images drive the warning.

greek_phrase: εἰ ἐπείρασεν ὁ θεὸς εἰσελθὼν λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ ἔθνος ἐκ μέσου ἔθνους
chosen_rendering: Has God attempted, entering in, to take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation
alternate_renderings: Has God tried to go and take...
rationale: Leaves the startling verb attempted visible and keeps the entering-in sequence active in the line.

greek_phrase: πρόσωπον κατὰ πρόσωπον
chosen_rendering: face to face
alternate_renderings: personally; openly
rationale: Best preserves the relational directness of the idiom.

greek_phrase: ἐπὶ ματαίῳ
chosen_rendering: in vain
alternate_renderings: on emptiness; for emptiness
rationale: English witness tradition is unanimous here, and in vain best carries the command idiom in English while the footnote preserves the emptiness nuance of the Greek.

greek_phrase: ὁ βλέπων
morphology: articular present active participle masculine singular
chosen_rendering: the seer
alternate_renderings: the one seeing; the observer
rationale: Keeps the older title distinct from prophet and matches the explanatory note in the verse itself.

greek_phrase: πνεῦμα κυρίου
morphology: nominative neuter singular noun + genitive noun
chosen_rendering: the Spirit of the Lord
alternate_renderings: the breath of the Lord; the wind of the Lord
rationale: Prophetic transformation context favors Spirit, while the dynamic verb preserves force.

greek_phrase: κέκρυπται ἐν τοῖς σκεύεσιν
morphology: perfect passive indicative 3 singular + dative plural noun
chosen_rendering: he is hidden among the baggage
alternate_renderings: among the gear; among the vessels
rationale: Baggage fits the scene of assembled tribal gear better than a literal vessels.

greek_phrase: φωνὰς καὶ ὑετόν
morphology: accusative plural noun + accusative singular noun
chosen_rendering: voices and rain
alternate_renderings: thunders and rain
rationale: Keeps the Greek wording literal while preserving the storm-sign theme.

greek_phrase: ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ
morphology: accusative noun + preposition + accusative noun phrase
chosen_rendering: a man according to his heart
alternate_renderings: a man after his heart; a man fitting his heart
rationale: Keeps the relational metaphor explicit and avoids collapsing it into a later interpretive slogan.

greek_phrase: οὐκ ἔστιν τῷ κυρίῳ συνεχόμενον σῴζειν ἐν πολλοῖς ἢ ἐν ὀλίγοις
chosen_rendering: for the Lord there is no restraint to save by many or by few
alternate_renderings: nothing hinders the Lord from saving by many or by few
rationale: Preserves both the saving action and the contrast between large and small means.

greek_phrase: ἰδοὺ ἀκοὴ ὑπὲρ θυσίαν ἀγαθή
chosen_rendering: hearing is better than sacrifice
alternate_renderings: obedient hearing is better than sacrifice
rationale: Uses hearing because the Greek stresses listening to the divine voice, with obedience implied by context. Existing English witnesses do not require smoothing away the hearing language.

greek_phrase: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ὄψεται εἰς καρδίαν
morphology: nominative noun + future middle verb + accusative phrase
chosen_rendering: God sees into the heart
alternate_renderings: God sees the heart; God looks into the heart

greek_phrase: τοις υιοις ιωσηφ υιοις εφραιμ κατα συγγενειας αυτων κατα δημους αυτων κατ' οικους πατριων αυτων κατα αριθμον ονοματων αυτων κατα κεφαλην αυτων παντα αρσενικα απο εικοσαετους και επανω πας ο εκπορευομενος εν τη δυναμει
chosen_rendering: As for the sons of Joseph, the sons of Ephraim, by their families, by their clans, by the houses of their fathers, by the number of their names, by their headcount, every male from twenty years old and upward, every one going out in force,
